title: Septic shock in children
subject: paediatrics
summary: Recognise sepsis early (Phoenix criteria), measure lactate, take cultures and give antimicrobials within 1 hour for suspected septic shock. Where ICU care exists, give 10 to 20 mL/kg balanced crystalloid boluses up to 40 to 60 mL/kg in the first hour (without ICU, no boluses unless hypotensive), then adrenaline or noradrenaline (SSC Children 2026).

sections.title: Recognise
items: Phoenix criteria (used by SSC Children 2026): sepsis is suspected infection with a Phoenix Sepsis Score of 2 or more (respiratory, cardiovascular, coagulation and neurological dysfunction).
Septic shock is sepsis with at least 1 cardiovascular point: severe hypotension for age, blood lactate 5 mmol/L or more, or need for vasoactive medication.

Hypoperfusion: tachycardia, prolonged capillary refill or flash refill, weak or bounding pulses, cold mottled or warm flushed peripheries, altered consciousness, reduced urine output. Hypotension is a late sign.
Higher risk: infants, severe malnutrition, immunocompromise, cancer, indwelling devices and recent hospital stay. In India also consider dengue, malaria, scrub typhus and enteric fever.

sections.title: First hour
items: Oxygen and airway support, IV or IO access within minutes, check glucose and ionised calcium, and measure blood lactate (strong recommendation).
Take blood cultures before antimicrobials when this does not substantially delay them.

Suspected septic shock: broad-spectrum antimicrobials as soon as possible, ideally within 1 hour. Probable sepsis without shock: rapid, time-limited assessment and antimicrobials within 3 hours if sepsis is substantiated.

Where intensive care is available: give up to 40 to 60 mL/kg as 10 to 20 mL/kg boluses over the first hour, reassessing after every bolus and stopping when shock resolves or signs of fluid overload appear (crackles, hepatomegaly, worsening work of breathing).

Where intensive care is not available: no fluid boluses for sepsis without hypotension (start maintenance fluids); for septic shock with hypotension give up to 40 mL/kg (10 to 20 mL/kg per bolus) in the first hour.

Prefer balanced crystalloid (Ringer lactate) over 0.9% saline, and crystalloid over albumin. 0.9% saline is acceptable if balanced fluid is unavailable and may be preferred with hyponatraemia or raised intracranial pressure.

sections.title: Vasoactive drugs and adjuncts
items: Start adrenaline or noradrenaline for fluid-refractory shock or when fluid overload limits boluses. SSC 2026 found insufficient evidence to prefer either drug or to fix a fluid volume before starting. Start through a peripheral line rather than waiting for central access.

In practice, many clinicians choose adrenaline for cold shock or myocardial dysfunction and noradrenaline for warm vasodilated shock. Use cardiac and lung point-of-care ultrasound to guide fluids and drugs if trained.
High-dose catecholamine requirement: add vasopressin or titrate catecholamines further.

Hydrocortisone: do not give if stability is restored with fluids and vasoactive drugs. Give stress-dose hydrocortisone for suspected or known adrenal insufficiency (long-term steroids, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, purpura fulminans); SSC 2026 makes no recommendation for refractory shock.
After initial resuscitation, titrate oxygen to SpO2 88 to 92% rather than above 94%. Avoid etomidate for intubation.
Achieve source control urgently (drain abscesses, remove infected lines once new access is secured). Do not routinely give vitamin C, thiamine, IVIG or levothyroxine.

sections.title: Targets and monitoring
items: Guide resuscitation by heart rate, blood pressure, capillary refill, skin temperature, pulse volume, consciousness and urine output; repeat lactate.
If a central venous catheter is in place, target ScvO2 of 70% or more.
Chart cumulative fluid balance. Once stable, avoid further excess fluid and consider diuretics or renal replacement therapy for fluid overload.

sections.title: Escalate
items: PICU for any vasoactive requirement, persistent hypoperfusion, respiratory failure or altered consciousness; call early for retrieval from district hospitals.

Refractory shock: look for an uncontrolled source, pneumothorax, tamponade, adrenal insufficiency, hypocalcaemia or hypoglycaemia. VA ECMO only as rescue where available; VV ECMO for refractory hypoxaemia.
Before transfer: secure the airway if needed, run vasoactive drugs through a dedicated line, record total fluids and drugs given, and send cultures and results with the child.

sections.title: Special groups
items: Severe acute malnutrition: use the SAM shock protocol (15 mL/kg over 1 hour with close monitoring), not rapid boluses.
Dengue: follow the national dengue fluid protocol for shock; avoid unnecessary boluses in the plasma leakage phase.
Neonates: use neonatal sepsis and shock guidance; avoid repeated blind fluid boluses.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Repeating boluses without reassessment, especially where ICU care is unavailable or in children with malnutrition, anaemia or heart disease.
Delaying antimicrobials for lumbar puncture, imaging or difficult cultures.
Waiting for hypotension before treating shock.
Not narrowing or stopping antimicrobials once culture results and clinical course are known.

drugs.name: Balanced crystalloid (Ringer lactate)
drugs.dose: 10 to 20 mL/kg IV per bolus; up to 40 to 60 mL/kg in the first hour where ICU is available, up to 40 mL/kg if hypotensive where it is not
drugs.notes: Reassess after every bolus; stop if overload.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine) infusion
drugs.dose: Start 0.05 to 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV, titrate to perfusion
drugs.notes: Cold shock or myocardial dysfunction; peripheral line acceptable initially.

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine) infusion
drugs.dose: Start 0.05 to 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV, titrate to perfusion and blood pressure
drugs.notes: Warm vasodilated shock; peripheral line acceptable initially.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone
drugs.dose: 2 mg/kg IV (max 100 mg) as a stat stress dose
drugs.notes: Only for suspected or known adrenal insufficiency; continue per endocrine advice.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: 100 mg/kg/day IV in 1 or 2 divided doses (max 4 g/day)
drugs.notes: Common empirical choice for community-acquired sepsis; adjust for source, local antibiogram and MDR risk.
